name: particle-cell-index-survives-floor-truncation-and-an-atomic-swap
rationale: Straight-line with three early returns and no loop, so execution_safety is loop_free. Every address in the kernel is a byte offset read out of the 35-entry particle_data_header, so the case sets exactly four of them: description 0 names the parameter block at 0, description 4 the position array at 1024, description 33 the atomic grid at 1088 and description 34 the next-index array at 1344. The parameter block gives a particle count of 1 (so the single thread's index 0 passes the bound), grid dimensions 4x4x4, a grid origin of zero, a cell size of 1 and cell strides (1, 4, 16). The one position is (1.5, 2.5, 3.5): dividing by the cell size and taking air.fast_floor.v3f32 gives (1.0, 2.0, 3.0), and air.convert.s.v3i32.f.v3f32 must truncate that to (1, 2, 3) -- the halves are there so a convert that rounded to nearest instead of truncating would land on (2, 3, 4) and pick a different cell. The two signed remainders that wrap negative cells leave (1, 2, 3) alone, so the linear index is 1*1 + 4*2 + 16*3 = 57. The grid is seeded with 1000+i, which makes the cell the shader chose readable from the output rather than inferred: air.atomic.global.xchg.i32 must leave 0 in grid[57] and return the 1057 that was there, and the flag byte at offset 896 is 1 so that return value is stored to next[0]. The other 63 grid slots must still read 1000+i and next[1..3] must still be 0xABABABAB, which is what says the atomic hit one slot and the store one word.

rationale: Reaching variant of the zero-selector case of this entry (TODO 6.2, WP-RVC), whose zero extents stop the kernel before its arithmetic. Constant 123 selects the float-query, int8-key/value path (input types 11, 1, 11: the 8x8 simdgroup-matrix instantiation) and constant 115 its multi-simdgroup-per-row form with a matrix mask, the AGX3 emask path, threadgroup tile 8 rows x 16 keys, simdgroup tiles 8x8, K tile 8 and threadgroup O reduction off, so the result is stored directly into oArray (binding 28) and the first context tile's normalized result goes through the O-sum workspace (binding 27). One threadgroup of two simdgroups; alpha 2, so every score is the int8 dot product times kScale x alpha = 0.5. This instantiation has no edge checks (its AGX3 accesses use full masks), so every extent is whole: queryLength 8 = the tile rows, contextLength 32 = two whole 16-key context tiles, dimsPerHead = paddedDimsPerHead = 16 = the tile width, and every buffer holds exactly the tile's reach; oArray holds the 8 x 16 result. Key n belongs to one of four groups; query row r holds 400 at its group's one-hot dimension plus small terms shared per group, so every key of the row's group scores the row maximum and every other key at least 176 below (exp underflows to 0 everywhere); the mask adds a row shift and removes (-1000) the row's group keys it does not keep. The kept keys per row and context tile keep every running sum a power of two (a row with no kept key in the first tile is rescaled by exp of at most -176 = 0), every softmax weight is 0 or exp(0) = 1, and each output is the V scale 0.5 times the mean of 1, 2, 4 or 8 small int8 values of V, exact. name: gemv-t-two-batches-36x8-tail-of-four
rationale:
MLX's transposed float32 GEMV, tiled bm1_bn2_sm8_sn4_tm4_tn1: out_vec[b][j] = sum over i of mat[b][i][j] * in_vec[b][i], with the column total assembled across eight lanes by three air.simd_shuffle_down.f32 stages.

One 64-thread threadgroup per batch, which on a 32-wide simdgroup is exactly the two simdgroups bn2 asks for: simd_gid selects the low or high half of the eight output columns and simd_lid splits into a row block (simd_lid >> 2, eight of them) and a column (simd_lid & 3, four of them). in_vec_size is 36 so that both row loops do real work and neither is dead: 36 / 32 is one, so the strided main loop runs a single iteration covering rows 0..31 across the eight row blocks, and the remainder 36 - 32 = 4 makes the tail loop run four times for row block 0 (rows 32..35) and exactly zero times for every other block, whose row start is already past 36. Dropping the tail would cost column j exactly 4766 + 8832*(j+1); dropping either of the two dispatched batches, or any single one of the 36 rows, changes a different column by a different amount.

Every value is a small integer, which is what makes an exact comparison legitimate here. mat[b][i][j] = (i+1) + 64*(j+1) + 1024*b is at most 1572, in_vec[0][i] = i+1 and in_vec[1][i] = -(i+1) are at most 36 in magnitude, so no product exceeds 56592 and no column total exceeds 1039182 -- all far inside binary32's exactly-representable integer range. The answer therefore does not depend on the order the eight lane partials are summed, nor on whether the multiply-add fuses, so a mismatch is a lowering difference rather than a rounding one. The closed forms are out_vec[0][j] = 16206 + 42624*(j+1) and out_vec[1][j] = -(698190 + 42624*(j+1)).

Two batches make the two 64-bit stride buffers load-bearing: batch 1's matrix is offset by 1024 per element and its vector is negated, so reading batch 0's matrix for batch 1 would return -58830 where -740814 is written, and reading batch 0's vector would flip the whole second half positive.

execution_safety is authored_bounded. Every reachable loop is bounded by an authored value: the main row loop by in_vec_size / 32 = 1, the tail loop by the four-row tile and the max(row_start, in_vec_size) - row_start guard, the two inner tile loops by the literal four, and the reduction by its own halving from four to one.

First coverage of air.is_uniform.i1 (433 case-less corpus sources, the largest uncovered count in the corpus). What this case does NOT pin is that symbol's answer. AIR feeds every air.is_uniform result straight to llvm.assume, here and in all 35143 corpus occurrences, so the program supplies the fact rather than observing it; the case proves the module still computes the right GEMV with the assertion lowered to the constant it asserts, but no authored input can make a wrong answer to it visible. air.simd_shuffle_down.f32 and air.wg.barrier are exercised and discriminated, and were already covered elsewhere. Buffers 2, 7, 8, 9, 10, 13 and 14 carry air.arg_unused and are bound with in-range literals.

name: sixteen-lanes-dequantize-through-the-public-linked-destination
rationale: Reaching variant of the single-lane case of this entry (TODO 6.2, WP-RVC), whose linked destination callback was the retained postfixPrimary_4xf, which writes nothing. This case links the public module validation/fixtures/public/linked/mps_postfix_primary_4xf_to_last_buffer (owned MSL, DESIGN D431 item 2): it stores the float4 at elements coordinate.x to coordinate.x + 3 of the kernel's buffer table's last array (constant 122 = 3 gives the kernel three arrays, and the callback the count 3), so each dequantized value reaches the destination. Sixteen threads (one threadgroup) each read 3 packed bytes of FP6 E2M3 codes at 3 * gid.x from array 0 and one scale byte at (4 gid.x) >> 5 from array 1 (E8M0 scale bytes 0x79 (0.015625), 0x84 (32), one per 32 elements); thread gid.x writes elements 4 gid.x to 4 gid.x + 3 of array 2 (256 bytes, poisoned 0xab before), so every thread's four words are observed and none overlaps another's. The codes spread over the format's nonzero finite encodings (no zero of either sign, whose sign the kernels' fast math leaves unspecified, and no NaN or infinity); every decoded value times its scale is a normal float, exact, 64 distinct words. Straight-line code: no loop.

name: gather-mm-rhs-nn-half-k40-two-experts
rationale: Reaching variant of the zero-shape case of this entry (TODO 6.2, WP-RVC), whose zero extents stop the kernel before its arithmetic. One threadgroup of 64 lanes (2 simdgroups) runs the single 16x64 output tile: B = 1, M = 16, N = 64, K = 40 (gemm_k_iterations_aligned = 2, remainder 8), M and N aligned (user constant 3): the two whole 16-deep blocks go through the unguarded loader and the 8-deep remainder through the guarded one; constant 122 binds a two-entry table. The indices select expert 0 for rows below 8 and expert 1 for the rest, so the kernel walks two row segments, each a full tile multiply over its expert (experts_stride_b = N*K = 2560), writing only its own rows. B[e][k][n] (ldb = 64): expert 0 holds q(n, k) = (11n + 3k + floor(3nk/5)) mod 16, nonlinear in n, so the 64 column sums differ, and expert 1 holds q/2. A[m][k] (lda = 40): rows of segment 0 hold a = 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 repeating along k, rows of segment 1 hold 2a, so every row of the result is the same (2a . q/2 = a . q): the linked destination callback, which writes table entry 1 at the column coordinate only, stores one value per column from every row, the same value, so the 64 words observed (256 bytes) do not depend on write order, and a row given the other segment's expert would write another. Every input is a multiple of 0.5 at most 15, exact in half; every product is a multiple of 0.5 at most 75 and every sum of 40 at most 3000, below 2^12: exact in float in any order or contraction. Every loop is finite by these inputs: the row-segment scan stops at M = 16, the K loop runs gemm_k_iterations_aligned = 2 times, the segment loop ends after the two segments, and the element loops have constant trip counts.

The destination holds 64 floats and two fill words that keep 0xab. Every loop is finite by these inputs: two key blocks, constant inner trip counts.

name: explicit-gradient-sample-at-texel-centres
rationale: Eight threads sample an 8x1 rgba32_float texture of one level with explicit gradients ((0.25, 0), (0, 0.25)) (sampler.sample_grad, DESIGN D213) at uv = ((g + 0.5) / 8, 0.5), the centre of texel g, through a runtime sampler that is nearest for minification and magnification, not mipmapped, and clamps to edge: whatever level of detail the gradients give, the one level's nearest texel is texel g. Texel x is (1.5x, -x, 0.125, 1), so out[g] is texel g. Texel 0's green lane is -0.0 (the -x of x = 0, sign bit set), so out[0]'s green lane is -0.0 as well: a nearest sample of a 32-bit float texel returns its value unconverted, the sign of a zero included, and the exact compare asks for that sign. The AIR has no loop.

name: wide-convert-and-math-leftovers
rationale: Sixteen air.* symbols the corpus reaches a handful of times each and that no authored case covered: air.convert.f.v16f32.f.v16f16, air.convert.f.v16bf16.f.v16f16, air.convert.f.v8bf16.f.v8f16, air.convert.f.v8f16.f.v8bf16, air.convert.f.v4bf16.f.v4f16, air.convert.f.v4f16.s.v4i32, air.powr.v4f16, air.max.u.v3i32, air.max.s.v3i32, air.abs.s.v3i32, air.fract.v2f16, air.fmin.v3f32, air.fmax.v3f32, air.floor.v3f16, air.fast_fmedian3.f32 and air.fast_cospi.f32. One thread, no loop, every argument read from a buffer so nothing folds. The half-to-bfloat rows carry the claim: half to binary32 is exact, so half to bfloat rounds exactly once, and the sixteen inputs walk every case of that rounding -- exact, down, up, a tie whose kept bit is even and a tie whose kept bit is odd, the largest half (which carries out to 65536), both zeros, both infinities, the smallest normal and two subnormals, since a half subnormal is an ordinary bfloat once bfloat's binary32 exponent range is available. The reverse direction has the opposite hazard: a bfloat's 8-bit significand always fits a half but its exponent range does not, so 1e30 becomes infinity and 1e-30 becomes zero. air.convert.f.v4f16.s.v4i32 asks two ties (2049 to 2048 and -2051 to -2052, both to even) and one overflow (70000 to infinity). max.u.v3i32 has 0xFFFFFFFF in lane 1 and max.s.v3i32 has a negative in lane 0, so each would answer the other's lane wrong if the comparison lost its signedness. fract lane 0 is the negated smallest normal half, where x - floor(x) rounds to 1 and Metal must clamp to the largest half below it. fmin and fmax have a NaN operand in lane 0, which both must ignore. The rows that cannot be asked exactly are asked where the answer is: powr at power-of-two bases with dyadic exponents so log2 and exp2 are both exact, cospi at the integers and one half-integer, and median3 is a pure selection so its fast variant cannot differ. Results are bit-cast into one uint buffer so a single output region carries every width without a conversion that would round.

name: atan2-at-every-pair-of-special-operands-without-fast-math
rationale: Thread 16 * j + k computes atan2(y_j, x_k) for every ordered pair of sixteen values per width: +0, -0, the smallest positive and negative denormals, the smallest normal, 1, -1, 3, -0.75, the largest positive and negative finites, both infinities, and three NaNs (positive and negative quiet, and 0x7fc12345 / 0x7e45 with a payload). It writes the float atan2(y, x), fast::atan2(y, x), the half atan2(y, x), and precise::atan2(y, x). Compiled without fast math, so no call carries nnan, ninf, or nsz and C99 Annex F defines the answers on the axes and at the infinities. Question (WP-FMX, DESIGN D253, for D208.7's atan2 special operands): which word Metal answers at each, NaN encodings and zero signs included, so that the translation can select those words exactly on every device.

name: a-union-member-store-lands-on-the-slot-it-names
rationale:
An MSL `union` lowers to a ONE-MEMBER LLVM struct -- `union { ulong u; float f; uint2 v; }` is `%union.Slot = type { i64 }` -- so a store through any member arrives with a `TypeStruct` pointee. `bitcast_width` has no answer for a struct, every width-based store rule declines, and the module used to be refused outright: `owned Store violates its pointer-pointee and value-type contract: pointer %74, of type %11 (TypePointer Function %6), points at %6 (TypeStruct %5), but the stored value is %79, of type %1 (TypeFloat 32)`. Every union member starts at byte offset 0 and a `Function` struct carries no explicit `Offset` decoration, so member 0 of a single-member struct is the slot's own address; `emitter::body::vector_store::emit_single_member_struct_store` descends to it and re-enters the store handler on the leaf.

The descent happens once, at the store dispatch, so it is the whole chain below it that has to be right -- not one rule. This case takes two different ones through it. `s[j].f` is a NARROWING member store: four bytes into an eight-byte slot, which Logical SPIR-V cannot express as a partial store, so `emit_scalar_narrowing_store` read-modify-writes and only the low half may change. `s[other].v` is a SAME-WIDTH one: `emit_same_width_reinterpret_store` bitcasts the `uint2` to the slot's `i64` and replaces all eight bytes. A descent that landed at the wrong address, or a read-modify-write that cleared the wrong half, moves a different word of the answer.

Two things about the shape are load-bearing and both were measured, not guessed. A scalar local is scalar-replaced by the frontend and the member store never reaches the emitter, so the slot has to be an array with a dynamic index. And the READ index has to be opaque to the frontend: reading back through `j` or `other` lets it forward both member stores to the load, which folds the answer to constants and leaves both stores dead -- observed on two earlier spellings of this kernel. Taking `r` from a second element of the input buffer defeats that, and the emitted AIR keeps one real `load i64` through a dynamic index.

The answer is derived, not blessed. Thread t writes 0xdeadbeefcafebabe into slot `in[t] & 1` and 0x0123456789abcdef into the other, narrows `(float)t + 0.5` over the first's low half, and stores `uint2(t + 3, 0xfeedface)` over the whole of the second. Threads 0..3 read the narrowed slot and threads 4..7 the vector one, so both stores are observed: the words are (0x3f000000, 0xdeadbeef), (0x3fc00000, 0xdeadbeef), (0x40200000, 0xdeadbeef), (0x40600000, 0xdeadbeef), then (7, 0xfeedface), (8, 0xfeedface), (9, 0xfeedface), (10, 0xfeedface). The 0xdeadbeef half is the narrowing assertion -- a full-width store or a read-modify-write that clears the wrong half loses it -- and the absence of any 0x01234567 or 0x89abcdef is the same-width one. Every float is exactly representable in binary32 and the output buffer starts all-zero, which no arm can produce.

`loop_free`: no loop and no call other than the `air.convert` intrinsic. One threadgroup of eight threads, half the length of the input.

name: float-five-vectors-six-rows-k256-simdgroup-reduction-direct-write
rationale: Reaching variant of dccb629e (linked-zero-work-ndarray-vector-matrix-multiply-5-8), whose zero kernelInfoBits (fcNumX 0) select none of the kernel's typed paths (TODO 6.2, WP-RVC). Constant 115 = 0x514000008146d94 selects the float path with five vectors: fcNumX 5, A, B and D float, A not transposed (A[row][k], ARowBytes 1040), B transposed (B[x][k], BRowBytes 1056), scalar B loads, K divisible by 4 and no partial-reduction tail, a K tile of one step, the simdgroup reduction (constant 127 = 0x40: the device supports it; not marked an Apple device, so the kernel takes its thread and threadgroup positions as dispatched), the row edge check, alpha applied, and the direct D write (no postfix linking, no write transpose). The params (binding 25) give N = 6 rows, K = 256, alpha = 0.5, DRowBytes 32, and 2 steps of 128 K elements (numDeviceReductions and its tile-K count; constant 124 = 0 keeps the params' counts). Threadgroups of 32 x 2 lanes over a 32 x 8 grid give row tgid.y * 2 + tid.y, one simdgroup per row: each lane multiplies its four consecutive A elements (4 tid.x + 128 step) with the same four elements of each of the five vectors, simd_sum adds the 32 lanes, and lane 0 writes D[row * 8 + x] = 0.5 * sum_k A[row][k] B[x][k] for x = 0 to 4. A[r][k] = (k^2 + 5k + 3r + rk) mod 7 - 3 and B[x][k] = (3k + 2x + 1 + (x + 1) floor(k / 7)) mod 5 - 2 (the row padding past K holds 64 and 32, never read). Rows 6 and 7 fail the edge check: they read the zero buffer (binding 24) and write nothing, and words 5 to 7 of every row are never written, so those keep the 0xab fill. Every product is an integer of magnitude at most 6 and every partial sum an integer of magnitude below 2^11, so each sum is exact in float in any order (fast-math reassociation and the simdgroup sum included) and none is zero; times 0.5 it stays exact. Expected D rows 0 to 5 (x = 0 to 4): [[-1.5, -0.5, 8.0, -238.5, 5.0], [4.5, 3.5, -2.5, -88.5, -4.5], [-3.5, 4.0, -6.0, 184.0, -3.5], [-1.0, 4.5, -2.5, -54.5, 1.0], [-2.0, 1.5, -2.5, -34.0, 2.0], [0.5, 2.0, 1.0, -272.5, 6.5]]. Every loop is bounded by these constants and params: 2 K steps, five vectors, constant trip counts elsewhere.

name: linked-zero-work-ndarray-vector-matrix-multiply-5-8
no_effect: The authored parameters give the work an empty extent, so the entry returns before any write reaches the selected output.
rationale: Zero matrix dimensions and disabled typed paths select no matrix work for the sole invocation. The poisoned destination is observed exactly and the direct callback uses an exact signature-compatible module. The four operand buffers at Metal indices 26 through 29 and the threadgroup reduction at index 0 are the int8 arm of this kernel's function-constant type selection: the packed 64-bit user constant is zero, so its type field ((fc115 >> 7) & 7) is 0, which is isAInt8 rather than isAFloat/isAHalf/isABFloat16, and each of those four location indices is shared by all four type variants with exactly one enabled. They are declared because reflection requires them, and they are 256 zero bytes each because the zero K parameter makes every accumulation count zero, so no element of A, B, C or D is read on this dispatch and the observed bytes come from the linked destination array instead. Replaced (DESIGN D296): the linked destination callback writes table entry 1, so the case binds a two-entry table (MPSNDArrayRefSize 1 source, 1 destination) whose destination element carries the source element's fill.

name: blend-two-uniform-cubes-and-write-one-face-of-a-third
rationale: The kernel turns each cube texel's own face and coordinate into a direction, rotates it by a float3x3 from the constant buffer, samples two cubes along it, mixes them by one buffer float and adds the first scaled by another, then writes the result to that face of a third cube. Both source cubes carry the same four halves in every texel of every face, so the direction the rotation produces cannot change what is sampled and the arithmetic is all that remains: at a blend of one half and a sum factor of one quarter the three colour lanes are 0.875, 0.4375 and 0.6875 exactly, and the alpha is the literal one the shader inserts rather than either source's -- both sources carry 9 and -9 there, so a swizzle that read it would be visible. All six faces are dispatched and all six are compared, so a write that lost its face operand would leave five faces holding their initial bytes.

name: rms-norm-scales-by-exactly-one-half-through-air-rsqrt
rationale: Both reduction loops are `for (int i = 0; i < N_READS; i++)` with N_READS a template constant of 4, so every loop in the AIR runs exactly four times regardless of input. axis_size is 16 and threads_per_threadgroup is 4, so lid*N_READS+N_READS is at most 16 and every thread takes the unchecked fast path. The point of the input is to make air.rsqrt.f32 exact: the four per-thread sums of squares are 32, 16, 8 and 8, air.simd_sum.f32 brings them to 64, eps is 0 and axis_size is 16, so the argument is exactly 4.0 and rsqrt is exactly 0.5 -- no reliance on a transcendental's low bits, and a wrong rsqrt cannot be hidden because inv_mean multiplies every one of the 16 outputs. w_stride is 1 and every x is 0, 2 or 4, so out[i] = w[i] * 0.5 * x[i] lands on 2, 4, 5..10, 13, 14 and six exact zeros. The zeros are load-bearing twice over: they pin that the four x values a thread reads are its own lid*4 slice and not another thread's, and the 0xAB fill makes any store the translator drops show up as 0xABABABAB rather than as a plausible float.

name: visible-table-clear-slots-two-through-twenty-five-2x1-output
rationale: One invocation calls visible-function-table slots 2 through 25 and receives exact float4 zero from all twenty-four linked _uber_clear bodies. A twenty-seven-word size table and eight explicit argument-info records keep every selector and offset in bounds; register 2 is selected. The complete 2x1 primary block at origin (2,0) is captured byte-exactly from the poisoned 4x1 resource.

name: visible-table-clear-slots-two-through-twenty-one-rgb-lane-output
rationale: One invocation calls visible-function-table slots 2 through 21 and receives exact float4 zero from all twenty linked _uber_clear bodies. A twenty-three-word size table and eight explicit argument-info records keep every selector and offset in bounds; register 2 is selected. This entry splats the selected R, G, and B lanes into the complete poisoned 3x1 primary footprint byte-exactly.

name: skybox-one-texel-1d-sample-saturates-alpha
rationale: Both function constants are false, so the dither and sRGB arms are statically dead and the fragment reduces to one air.sample_texture_1d.v4f32 scaled by intensity.x. The one-texel 1D texture makes the sample independent of the harness-fixed uv varying that supplies its coordinate, and the ClampToEdge linear sampler blends that single texel with itself. Intensity is exactly one and the texel lanes (0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 2.0) are all exact in binary32 and binary16, so the float-to-half convert and the scale are both lossless. The alpha of two is out of range on purpose: air.saturate.f16 clamps it, so the returned (0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1.0) both pins the clamp and keeps four distinct lanes against a swap.
